items.heading: Article 2

items.text: 1. This Directive applies to children who are suspects or accused persons in criminal proceedings. It applies until the final determination of the question whether the suspect or accused person has committed a criminal offence, including, where applicable, sentencing and the resolution of any appeal.

provisions.comment: The Juvenile Courts Act is lex specialis in relation to the Criminal Procedural Act, so all the rights guaranteed by the CPA and the JCA are applied from the earliest moment when a child is suspected in the criminal proceedings.
provisions.textEn: The provisions of the Penal Code, Criminal Procedure Act, Courts Act, Protection of Persons with Mental Disorders Act, laws governing the enforcement of sanctions for criminal offences and other general regulations shall be applied only if not regulated otherwise by this Act.

items.text: 2. This Directive applies to children who are requested persons from the time of their arrest in the executing Member State, in accordance with Article 17.

provisions.textEn: Jurisdiction of a juvenile court over a minor offender shall cease when such minor reaches twenty three years of age.

In criminal proceedings against a minor perpetrator who has not attained the age of twenty-three, the provisions of this Act and the provisions of the Criminal Procedure Code shall apply, unless they are contrary to the provisions of this Act.

A minor shall be a person whose age, at the time when the offence was committed, was between fourteen and eighteen, and a young adult shall be a person whose age, at the time when the offence was committed, was between eighteen and twenty one.

The provisions of Article 53, Article 53a (3) to (7), Article 53b, Article 54 (1) and (3), Articles 55 and 56, Article 60 (1), Article 63 to Article 68, Article 86 of this Act shall not apply in proceedings against the perpetrator who has reached the age of twenty-one at the time of the proceedings.

With regard to young adult perpetrators of criminal offences, the provisions of Penal Code and criminal-law provisions of other laws of the Republic of Croatia, and, subject to the requirements specified by this Act (Article 105), the provisions covering minor perpetrators of criminal offences shall be applicable.

The court may apply to a young adult a correctional measure of special obligations, correctional measure of intensified supervision and juvenile imprisonment. If the offender was, during the trial, under twenty one years of age, a reformatory measure can also be applied to him or her. The court shall apply a juvenile sanction when, having in mind the type of criminal offence and the manner in which it was committed, it may be concluded that such offence reflects, to a great extent, the perpetrator’s age, and the circumstances related to his or her personality support the belief that the purpose of the sanction will be accomplished by the application of correctional measures or by the imposition of the punishment of juvenile imprisonment. The applied correctional measure may not continue after the time when the perpetrator attains twenty three years of age.

Criminal proceedings against a young adult shall be conducted in accordance with the provisions of the Criminal Procedure Act, provided that in the proceedings against a perpetrator who is during the trial under twenty three years of age, the provisions of Article 56, Article 58, Article 74, Paragraph 1 and Article 78 of this Act shall apply. However, if it is established that the application of juvenile criminal law is available (Article 105), the provisions of Article 54, Paragraph 2 , Articles 57 and 59, Articles 60, Paragraphs 2 and 3, Articles 67, Paragraphs 1 and 3, Articles 71 to 73, Articles 89 and 93 of this Act shall be appropriately applicable.

items.comment:
The juvenile criminal law applies in Croatia to children who were under age of 18 when the offence was committed and who did not reach the age of twenty-three. However, it must not but can be applied also to so called young adults perpetrators who were 18 to 21 years of age when they have committed offence until they reach twenty three years of age (Articles 104, 105 and 107).

The provisions excepted from the application to the accused that has reached the age of 18, are also excluded in the Croatian law (Article 48(2))

provisions.comment: Provision of Article 208 paragraph 5 CPA regulates situation where a person, informally questioned by the police in a capacity of a “citizen”, or presumptive witness, becomes a suspect as defined in Article 122 CPA during the questioning. That person may no longer be questioned informally, i.e., without being warned of his/her rights, including the right to a defence counsel. If the police fail to comply with this provision, the statement given by the suspect, as well as all the evidence obtained as a result of that statement, cannot be used as evidence and must be excluded from the case file (Article 208.a paragraph 8 CPA).
provisions.textEn: If while police collecting information from a person, appear grounds for suspicion that that person committed or participated in the commission of a criminal offence, the police shall cease collecting information. The police may no longer collect information from that person but may instead question him/her in his/her capacity as suspect under the provisions of Article 208.a of this Act.

items.text: In any event, this Directive shall fully apply where the child is deprived of liberty, irrespective of the stage of the criminal proceedings.

provisions.textEn: (1) The procedural provisions of this Act shall establish rules which, before municipal courts and all other bodies conducting misdemeanor proceedings, ensure fair conduct of misdemeanor proceedings, protection of human rights, proper establishment of facts and lawful decision-making on misdemeanor liability so that no innocent person is convicted, and that the perpetrator of the misdemeanor be sentenced or another misdemeanor sanction is applied.

(3) If this Act does not contain provisions on certain issues of procedure, the provisions of the Criminal Procedure Act and the Juvenile Courts Act shall be applied in an appropriate manner, when appropriate to the purpose of the misdemeanor procedure.

(1) A person arrested or detained on suspicion of having committed a misdemeanor must be immediately informed of the reasons for the arrest or detention, at his request the competent authority shall inform his family or another person designated by him of the arrest or detention, and if questioned as a suspect or the defendant and to teach that she is not obliged to testify and that she has the right to the professional assistance of a defense counsel of her choice.

(2) Arrest or detention is considered to be any measure or action that includes deprivation of liberty of a person suspected of having committed a misdemeanor.

items.comment: The Misdemeanor Act in Art. 86 lists the rights of the arrested or detained person. These rights do not cover all the rights from the Directive. However, there is an additional provision of Art. 82(3) which stipulates that the provisions of the Criminal Procedure Act and the Juvenile Courts Act shall be applied in an appopriate manner, when appropriate to the purpose of the misdemeanor procedure, if the MA does not contain provisions on certain issues of procedure. Therefore, it can be concluded that Directive applies fully when the child is deprived of liberty.

items.heading: Article 3

provisions.textEn: “Child” shall mean a person under the age of eighteen years.

provisions.comment: This provision relates only to victims but Croatia does not have same provision for a child perpetrator.
provisions.textEn: Where the age of the victim is unknown and it is probable that the victim has not yet turned eighteen, it shall be presumed that the victim is a child.

Parental care consists of the responsibilities, duties and rights of the parents, for the purpose of protecting and promoting the child's personal and property rights and well-being. Parents are obliged to provide parental care in accordance with the child's developmental needs and opportunities.

Both the consenting parent or the parent exercising parental care of the child may temporarily entrust the day-to-day care of the child, including placement, to a person who fulfills the requirements laid down in this Act for the guardian.

Both parents consensually or the parent who is holder of parental care may entrust the everyday care of the child, including the placement of the child, in accordance with the decision of the Social Welfare Center and a special regulation governing social welfare, to the foster family or other natural or legal person performing the social welfare activity in accordance with the regulations governing social welfare.
Custody is a form of protection for a child without parental care, a person deprived of legal capacity and a person who is unable for other reasons to protect his/her rights and interests.
Parental care of the guardian child is replaced by custody.
Custody activities are performed by the social welfare center, guardian and special guardian in accordance with this Law.
“Child” shall mean a person under the age of eighteen years.

items.heading: Article 6

items.text: 1. Children who are suspects or accused persons in criminal proceedings have the right of access to a lawyer in accordance with Directive 2013/48/EU. Nothing in this Directive, in particular in this Article, shall affect that right.
items.comment: The Juvenile Courts Act does not explicitly state (in Article 1.a JCA) that the Directive 2013/48/EU is transposed into Croatian legal system through its provisions. However, as the CPA applies subsidiary (Article 3 JCA), the Directive is implicitly transposed through its provisions.

items.text: 2. Member States shall ensure that children are assisted by a lawyer in accordance with this Article in order to allow them to exercise the rights of the defence effectively.

provisions.textEn: The juvenile must have a defense counsel from the first action taken on grounds of suspicion that s/he committed the criminal offense until the criminal proceedings are finally terminated, when deciding to replace the correctional measure with the correctional institution measure and at the subsequent pronouncement of juvenile imprisonment.

If, in the cases referred to in paragraph 1 of this Article, the juvenile or persons authorized to take a defense counsel within the meaning of the provisions of the Criminal Procedure Act do not take a defense coiunsel, the judge shall appoint him/her ex officio.

items.comment:
The JCA prescribes mandatory defence in criminal proceedings against juvenile. There is a principal provision on mandatory defence, also guaranteeing the right to defence counsel throughout the entire proceedings (Article 54(1) JCA). The right to exercise that right effectively is guaranteed within numerous provisions that will be analyzed below.


Even if the rule on mandatory defence applies in general, the JCA provides an exception if the state attorney decides on the ground of principle of discretionary prosecution (Article 72 JCA). In that case, the minor has the right to defence counsel (Article 54(2) JCA), but the defence is not mandatory.

(1) The police are authorized to arrest a juvenile under the conditions specified in Article 107 of the Criminal Procedure Act and must immediately, and no later than within the time limit referred to in Article 109, paragraph 2 of the Criminal Procedure Act, bring him into custody or release him. The juvenile judge shall examine the arrested juvenile within twelve hours of his surrender to the custody supervisor. The state attorney and the defence counsel must be present at this interrogation.

Article 20

The detainee is provided with the needs of health care in accordance with the general regulations on health care. As a rule, the provision of health care is carried out through emergency medical teams, which will, after the examination, determine the possible need to provide health care to a detainee in a particular health institution.

The detainee will be allowed, under medical supervision, to undergo the medical therapy he started before the detention measure was ordered.

With the approval of the competent state attorney or the investigating judge, the detainee may, at his own expense, procure other medicines that can be given to him under the supervision and according to the instructions of the medical doctor.

Detained pregnant women are provided with special health care.

The detainee or his defence counsel may request the competent state attorney to undertake additional medical examinations.

Surgical and other medical interventions against a detainee may be undertaken only with his prior consent, and in the case of a minor, with the prior consent of a parent or guardian.

Exceptionally, in emergencies where a detainee's life is in danger, surgical and other medical interventions may be undertaken without prior consent, if the person is in such a state that he or she cannot decide on his or her own, or if the consent of a parent or guardian cannot be obtained.

If a detainee is suspected of suffering from an acute or infectious disease requiring treatment or isolation, the general regulations shall be followed.

The detention supervisor shall enter the data on the procedure related to the provision of medical care in the Detainee's Record.

The detainee may, with the approval of the competent public prosecutor or the investigating judge, be visited and examined by a doctor of his choice.

In urgent cases, the detention supervisor decides on the transfer of detainees to the appropriate medical institution, and without delay informs the competent state attorney and the organizational unit of the police that made the arrest.

The manner of exercising the rights referred to in Article 20 of this Ordinance, as well as the implementation of the measures referred to in paragraphs 1 and 2 of this Article, shall be organized and supervised by the custody supervisor.

Detention must be carried out in such a way as not to offend the person and dignity of the detainee, while preserving his physical and mental health, taking care to fulfill the purpose for which detention was ordered and to maintain the necessary order in the detention police unit.
The detainee will be provided with the necessary health care immediately.

The detainee must be provided with the possibility of maintaining personal hygiene.

The detainee shall be provided with other clothing and footwear if it is significantly damaged or hygienically unusable.

Procurement of other clothing and / or footwear will be provided by the police. The police may, in agreement with the detainee, obtain other clothing and / or footwear from his family or another person designated by him.

During the detention, the detainee is provided with food that must meet hygienic and nutritional standards in terms of quantity and quality.

Detainees eat their daily meals in their rooms or in appropriate common areas, as determined by the detention supervisor.

The detainee is provided with at least three meals a day, one of which must be a full meal.

Sick detainees receive food whose caloric value and composition are determined by a doctor.

During detention, the detainee must be provided with a continuous rest period of at least eight hours every twenty-four hours.

Supervision regarding the satisfaction of the conditions of nutrition and rest of detainees is performed by the detention supervisor.

(4) If the minor has not selected another suitable adult or if in relation to that other relevant adult selected by the minor there are circumstances referred to in paragraph 3 of this Article that have not been accepted by the body conducting the procedure or conducting the action , that authority shall request the appointment of a special guardian for the minor to accompany him during the actions in accordance with paragraphs 1 and 2 of this Article.

items.text: Where the child has not nominated another appropriate adult, or where the adult that has been nominated by the child is not acceptable to the competent authority, the competent authority shall, taking into account the child's best interests, designate another person to accompany the child. That person may also be the representative of an authority or of another institution responsible for the protection or welfare of children.

items.heading: Article 16
items.subHeading: Right of children to appear in person at, and participate in, their trial

items.text: 1. Member States shall ensure that children have the right to be present at their trial and shall take all necessary measures to enable them to participate effectively in the trial, including by giving them the opportunity to be heard and to express their views.

provisions.textEn: (1) A minor cannot be tried in absentia.

(1) At the session of the panel, the president of the panel shall determine the identity of the minor, in addition to the information on previous sanctions, shall inform him of the rights referred to in Article 239 (1) of the Criminal Procedure Act and shall ensure that the juvenile has understood the instruction on rights.

(2) After the State Attorney presents the description of the offence and the evidence on which the proposal for imposing an educational measure or for punishing a minor is based, the President of the panel shall instruct the juvenile that he may, but need not, make a statement about the commission of the criminal offence from the proposal of the State Attorney. If the juvenile does not make a statement about this, the court will take that he denies the commission of the crime.

(1) At the panel session the public prosecutor, minor, defence counsel, parents of minor or guardian, the victim and the injured, a representative of the social welfare institution and expert collaborator of the court shall be invited.

(2) The minor will always be taught orally in an understandable way about the meaning of the rights from the instruction. It is the duty of the authority taking action to ensure that the minor has understood the instruction on rights.

items.comment: The children always have to be present at trial since they cannot be tried in absentia. The Juvenile Courts Act provides that a child is aware of his rights and understands them. However, there is no obligation of the authority taking action to instruct the minor what would be the best conduct in a concrete situation, but it is compensated by the defence counsel.

items.text: 2. Member States shall ensure that children who were not present at their trial have the right to a new trial or to another legal remedy, in accordance with, and under the conditions set out in, Directive (EU) 2016/343.

items.comment: Since the Juvenile Courts Act does not provide for in absentia trials of children, it is not needed to implement this provision.

- the right to inform the legal representative of the child of all the rights of the child referred to in Article 24, paragraph 3 of this Act and this paragraph, and the right to accompany the legal representative of the child during the procedure,

- the right to protection of privacy, the right to medical examination and medical assistance,

- the right to restrict imprisonment and the use of alternative measures, including the right to periodic review of detention.

(2) The detention supervisor shall immediately inform the juvenile judge, the state prosecutor, the legal representative of the child and the social welfare center of the arrest of the person referred to in paragraph 1 of this Article and at the same time record this in the appropriate records.

(3) The Attorney General shall order that the requested person referred to in paragraph 1 of this Article be brought to the juvenile judge of the competent county court within 16 hours of arrest for examination within the meaning of Article 24 paragraph 3 of this Act.

(4) Unless otherwise provided by this Law, proceedings before a judge of investigation and proceedings before an extra-judicial panel shall be conducted with appropriate application of regulations governing the treatment of juvenile offenders.

(5) The procedure shall be carried out while securing the right to accompany the legal representative of the child and during the hearing before the court.

items.heading: Article 18

provisions.textEn: (1) The juvenile must have a defence attorney from the first action taken on grounds of suspicion that he committed the criminal offense until the criminal proceedings have been legally concluded, when deciding to replace the correctional measure with a facility correctional measure and at the subsequent imposition of juvenile prison.

(3) If, in the cases referred to in paragraph 1 of this Article, the juvenile himself or the persons authorized to take a defense lawyer within the meaning of the provisions of the Criminal Procedure Code do not take a defence lawyer, he shall be appointed ex officio by a juvenile judge.

items.comment: The Juvenile Courts Act requests that children who are suspects or accused persons in criminal proceedings have a defence attorney throughout the proceedings. Thus, the right to legal aid is also ensured and the question of the costs of legal aid will be resolved in the final judgement.

items.text: Member States shall ensure that children who are suspects or accused persons in criminal proceedings and children who are requested persons have an effective remedy under national law in the event of a breach of their rights under this Directive.

(2) A prisoner may file an oral or written complaint against the decision, measure or procedure of the warden or other prison officer whom the prisoner considers to be unlawfully deprived or restricted of his right to the president of the court that ordered the pre-trial detention for the purpose of obtaining protection against provable violations of his rights during pre-trial detention (hereinafter: the competent court). items.heading: Article 20

items.text: 1. Member States shall ensure that staff of law enforcement authorities and of detention facilities who handle cases involving children, receive specific training to a level appropriate to their contact with children with regard to children's rights, appropriate questioning techniques, child psychology, and communication in a language adapted to the child.

provisions.textEn: (1) Police authority over minors, young adults and in matters of health, development and upbringing and criminal law protection of children shall be exercised by a specially trained police officer for juveniles, who shall take care to protect the best interests of minors and protect their privacy.

The Ministry in charge of Justice and the Judicial Academy provide conditions for professional development of persons working in juvenile delinquency and criminal protection of children, organizes in cooperation with courts, state attorney's offices, scientific-educational institutions and lawyers' associations occasional professional consultations, seminars, knowledge tests and other forms of additional professional training of judges, state attorneys and other professionals in these jobs.

items.comment: Croatia explicitly prescribed that only specially trained police officers for youth can treat children. However, unlike the Directive, it did not prescribe which specific training these persons must undergo.

Without prejudice to judicial independence and differences in the organisation of the judiciary across the Member States, and with due respect for the role of those responsible for the training of judges and prosecutors, Member States shall take appropriate measures to ensure that judges and prosecutors who deal with criminal proceedings involving children have specific competence in that field, effective access to specific training, or both.

provisions.textEn: Juvenile judges and juvenile state attorneys must have a strong preference for the upbringing, needs and benefits of juveniles and have a basic knowledge of criminology, social pedagogy, youth psychology and social work for young people.
